What this proves

A concurrent execution race pays once. Replays are rejected. Confirmed transfer failures restore an approval. Only its owner can refund or change the executor.

Where the boundary is

This is a testnet prototype, not an audited financial product. A deployer upgrade key still exists. Protection applies per job ID; a new ID is a new approval.

From approval
to paid.

A payment tool for humans and the agents they authorize.

THE WORKFLOW
01 — 04
01

Connect a testnet wallet.

Use Meteor Wallet on testnet. Create a separate test account and fund it with test NEAR. Your wallet approves transactions; PayoutLatch never asks for your seed phrase.

Open testnet wallet ↗
02

Approve the exact payment.

Give the work a unique reference, choose an existing recipient and enter a NEAR amount. Optionally name an executor account for your agent. The wallet deposit is the principal plus a retained 0.02 NEAR storage reserve. Network gas is additional.

03

Release it—or delegate.

Open the job and release it yourself, or share its job ID with the named executor. The executor can call the contract’s execute method from code or this interface. It cannot change the amount or recipient.

Agent integration instructions ↗
04

Follow the chain state.

Pending means the transfer is in flight. Paid means the callback confirmed delivery. If delivery fails, Approved means you may retry or cancel. Cancellation returns the principal to its original owner; storage and gas are not refunded.

The details that matter.

Why NEAR testnet?

The hackathon FAQ allows testnet-only projects in every track. This prototype uses a native NEAR contract, not a mainnet-only integration. Testnet lets reviewers exercise the complete flow without real-money exposure.

Can I undo a payment?

Only an Approved job can be cancelled. Paid transfers are final. While a transfer or refund is pending, the contract rejects another attempt. There is no manual force-unlock.

What does the executor get permission to do?

Only execute that job. Its recipient and amount are fixed. The owner can replace or revoke the executor while the job is Approved. The executor does not receive the owner’s wallet key.

Is PayoutLatch an AI agent?

PayoutLatch is the payment-control contract and interface. It includes a command-line executor that any agent can call. It does not claim to judge work quality or run an autonomous AI model.
